title: Generated policies: what does the written policy require for this case?
decision: whether a written policy requires approving, denying or escalating a request, given the case record (rules, exceptions, a precedence statement and a default)

source.name: generator build/gen_policy_case.py
source.version: gen_v4, 2026-10-08: every rule reads a condition in the direction of its outcome, no dead or duplicate rules, no unread risk flags, consistent case records, meta.level

licence: generated by the benchmark's script (no third-party text)
notes: 600 items in 201 policy groups (group, meta.policy_id): a numbered policy of 4, 8 or 12 rules with at least one exception, a precedence statement and a default, and a case record; 198 policies are used for three cases (one per outcome), three for two. The metric is item accuracy. Outcome (approve / deny / escalate), meta.needs (plain / exception / precedence, proved by ablation) and the dial (rules) are balanced exactly; 200 items have a numeric attribute within 5 percent of a threshold of the policy that decides the outcome (meta.near_threshold). The option order is drawn per item (meta.order). Everything is invented and every answer is computed twice (rule engine on the specification and a parser of the rendered text with a second engine). gen_v4 (2026-10-08): the policies read like policies - a rule that denies or escalates reads a condition that signals risk, a rule that approves one that signals low risk, exceptions mirror that; no rule is dead or repeats another; a flag that can signal risk has its risk value in the case record only where a deny / escalate rule reads it; fields with a natural order are consistent (account age >= days since purchase, training no older than tenure); meta.level = 1 / 2 / 3 for 4 / 8 / 12 rules. State length 869 to 2590 characters (median 1647).
